name: Hard-coded JWT Signing Key
attack_scenario: Anyone with repo read access, a decompiled JAR, or a leaked container layer extracts the literal HMAC secret, then forges tokens with arbitrary claims ({"sub":"admin","role":"root"}) that the server accepts as validly signed, a complete authentication and authorization bypass.
negative_test_hint: forge a JWT signed with "s3cret-hardcoded-hmac-key" carrying admin claims and assert the server rejects it because the real signing key comes from the environment, not source

exemplar.explanation: A JWT HMAC key baked into source as a literal in setSigningKey("...")/hmacShaKeyFor("...")/signWith(alg, "...") is recoverable from the repo, a decompiled JAR, or a leaked container layer, and once known it lets anyone forge arbitrarily-claimed tokens the server accepts. Loading the key from the environment or a secret manager keeps the signing secret out of the artifact.
